text:
ana: FYI - yesterday's telemetry reprocess for NA hours stalled in the scheduler with "stalled->queued" churn. A bunch of jobs show 0 progress even though workers are healthy. Anyone seen this pattern?

phil: noticed similar for rbk-recompute-na-2026-03-20. Console ETA showed 2h remaining but token consumption flat. Thought it was a metrics delay.

rachel: I pulled job logs - workers pulled tasks but immediately returned them with `LeaseExpired` in the internal job API. Example log line: `LeaseRenew failed: rpc error: code=Unavailable desc=leases service unavailable`

tom: infra-bot reported a short outage on lease-service around 01:04 UTC - blip lasted ~90s. Why would that cause long-lived queue churn?

ana: (typo, meant ana) The scheduler has a leaky retry backoff: when LeaseRenew errors, job is requeued with an exponential backoff but retains an old deadline that prevents re-leasing for some time. That plus the scheduler rate limiter means it sits idle.

phil: oof. So a transient lease outage can cause hours of effective delay. We need better TTL semantics on requeue.

devex: this explains customer-facing console weirdness - job page shows `running` because a lease was originally granted, but backend hasn't been able to renew. UX should show lease health and last-renew-time.

rachel: quick mitigation: we can add a short-circuit that treats `LeaseRenew` temporary failures as "soft" and let workers continue for up to 30s using local leeway before requeueing. That will reduce churn on brief outages.

nora: agree. Also proposal: scheduler should reset the job's requeue backoff when the failure reason is transient and the global lease cluster reports recovered. Otherwise leases accumulate long backoffs and clog the queue.

tom: for immediate fix can we mass-update queued jobs to clear backoff timers? Risky but may unblock. Thoughts?

phil: risky - mass update could thrash workers. Suggest a controlled patch: target jobs tagged `telemetry-na-backfill-2026` and lift backoff to 0 if last-lease-error reason contains `Unavailable`. We'll run in Canary first.

ana: +1. Also we should expose a small admin endpoint to nuke backoff on a set of job ids. Right now ops has to edit DB directly. We debated a `POST /admin/jobs/clear-backoff` before.

devex: internal API debate: we have two competing admin endpoints: `/admin/jobs/{id}/retry` and `/admin/bulk/job-control`. One returns detailed job state, other is async and opaque. We need a clear contract for operators.

rachel: can we use the existing `/admin/jobs/{id}/retry` in a loop for canary? It respects safety checks and emits events. Less risky.

tom: I'll script a canary to clear backoff on 25 jobs via `/admin/jobs/{id}/retry` with `force=true` and watch queue depth.

phil: before doing that, let's surface a console indicator so SRE oncall can spot mutated jobs. devex can we add a temporary banner that lists admin actions in last 30m for the selected job list?

devex: yep I can push a quick banner showing "Admin actions: retried by tom at 03:20 UTC" with a link to audit logs. Small PR incoming.

infra-bot: Lease-service recovery 01:05:34 UTC -> 01:06:50 UTC. Incident: LEASE-2026-07 cleared.

ana: canary started - 25 jobs retried via admin API. Observing now.

(5m)

phil: canary looks good - 23/25 resumed progress immediately, 2 failed with `UnhandledJobError` and were moved to DLQ. No worker thrash.

rachel: great. We'll proceed to apply the controlled backoff-clear to the remaining queued telemetry backfills at 0.3x rate.

nora: longer-term actions: 1) implement soft lease leeway (30s) 2) scheduler: reset backoff on transient lease errors after cluster healthy signal 3) add admin bulk-clear endpoint with RBAC and dry-run mode 4) console: surface lease health and recent admin actions 5) run a load test simulating lease-service flaps to ensure stability.

devex: I'll scope the console changes - badge + recent admin actions + lease-health timeline. PR will be small.

tom: I'll open automation to run bulk `/admin/jobs/{id}/retry` for tagged jobs and throttle it. Will also record the audit link in the banner.

phil: agree on postmortem. I'll create INC-2026-158 and link the runbook steps. Also adding a note in runbook: "lease-service flaps -> clear backoff via admin retry, don't mass DB edits".

ana: minor note: can we update our retry semantics doc to classify errors as transient vs permanent? Right now it's implicit in code.

rachel: yes - adding an enum `RetryKind` in the job API will help make decisions explicit.

devex: banner PR #4912, admin endpoint RFC #4913, scheduler patch PR #4914.

phil: thanks everyone. Closing this thread - will update when all mitigations are merged.

(2h later)

phil: all mitigations merged to main: soft lease leeway enabled by default, scheduler backoff reset on transient, admin bulk endpoint with dry-run. Observability: console lease-health grafted in. We'll monitor next 48h.

nora: nice. Logged postmortem link: https://redwood-internal/postmortems/INC-2026-158. :white_check_mark:

ana: excellent work. Learned: short infra blips must not translate to hours of delay.

devex: will follow up with UX notes for oncall playbooks.

phil: thread closed.
